text: All parasites develop through an egg-larva-adult cycle. A direct cycle needs only one host animal to complete all stages — for example Ascaris in pigs: after eggs are eaten, larvae in the intestine migrate through the blood to the liver, then to the lungs and trachea, are swallowed, and return to the intestine where they mature into egg-laying adults, the whole cycle taking 2 weeks to 2 months; eggs (needing a microscope to see in feces) and sometimes whole adults are then excreted. An indirect cycle needs a second host species to complete — for example Fasciola (liver fluke) in cattle needs both a cow/buffalo and a snail: the snail sheds a larval stage onto grass, which after being eaten migrates to the liver, matures into an adult, and lays eggs that pass out in the feces to continue the cycle through a new snail.
